fields.why: Tables 1 and 2 are two-way cross-tabulations (missed-opportunity category by region, by race/ethnicity, by prenatal care), with no comparison within levels of a third variable. A followed the authors' word 'stratified', and its own notes concede they are two-way cross-tabs.

The report's analysis and headline ('gaps... in all U.S. Census Bureau regions and among all racial and ethnic groups') compare missed-opportunity distributions across 4 regions and 9 race/ethnicity groups (group). A's 2022 vs 2021 pair (31.7% increase) is a defensible but contextual primary contrast.
Scale follows the framework: the region and race shares are only set side by side (null), while the year contrast is a percent increase (relative). B's null is preferred given the group framework.

The P&S syphilis rates are restricted to 'females aged 15–44 years', so age and sex define a population. The brief records age always (and sex by the same rule), so A missed them; the level (2) is unaffected.

brief_issues: Readers may take 'stratified' in the authors' wording as stratified/adjusted; the brief could say that a two-way cross-tab by an SPD is comparison, whatever the authors call it. B's notes contradict its own record (they say stratified/adjusted was recorded and that 2022 vs 2021 is the primary contrast).
